Data Centers

Technology Services for Data Center Operators

Data center operators adding AI-specific capacity face a different operations model than traditional enterprise compute: GPU-to-GPU traffic is latency-sensitive, fabric health becomes a first-class signal, and security has to cover both the tenant environment and the infrastructure layer. TechnoKraft’s AI Data Center & AI Infrastructure practice is built for that reality.

How we engage

Engagements cover GPU cluster networking, InfiniBand and RDMA, high-speed Ethernet fabric, Rocky Linux environments, monitoring that correlates GPU and network signals, and NOC/SOC functions coordinated with the Cybersecurity practice.

US operators also face power, cooling and density constraints that shape architecture choices. Capacity planning is part of the engineering conversation, not a separate afterthought.

Staffing for GPU networking and AI operations roles is drawn from the same technical bar used on TechnoKraft delivery teams — practitioners screen practitioners.

In practice

  • Monitoring is designed around tightly coupled training jobs, not CPU-bound server fleets alone.
  • Security and network operations for the same environment are not split across disconnected vendors.
  • Managed services are available where an operator prefers an operating partner to a fully in-house team.

Common engagement triggers

  • Standing up or scaling GPU capacity
  • Fabric performance issues under real training load
  • Need for integrated NOC and SOC coverage
  • Hiring specialized GPU networking talent on a deadline
